newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican "Narco Granny" put behind bars.
newsitem.headline: Mexican "Narco Granny" put behind bars.

text.p: An 82-year-old woman was jailed on Tuesday for peddling drugs to schoolchildren in this industrial northern Mexican city, judicial officials said.

Christened the "Narco-Granny" by local media, Sofia Elena Garcia Caudillo was recently nabbed by police with 14 marijuana cigarettes in her posession. She confessed to having sold drugs to students, aged between 13 and 17, for 11 years.
A judge ordered Garcia to remain in jail without bond until sentencing -- a process that usually takes longer than a year, prison officials said.
Although there is a local law that prevents the sick or elderly from serving prison sentences, Garcia was denied bail because selling drugs is a federal crime, officials said.

A poor, wrinkled woman who wears torn clothes and leather sandals, Garcia became prisoner number 196 at the Topo Chico federal prison, where about 2,760 other inmates, many of them dangerous criminals, are also held.
When asked if a Reuter reporter could interview her, the woman reportedly told her guard, "I don't want anything to do with the press."
Although Mexican prisons are notoriously dirty and rife with corruption and crime, Topo Chico prison officials said they would take care of the elderly woman.
"She is doing just fine. She doesn't look in a bad state, but if she needs anything, we are going to help her," said Rodolfo Presa, director of the prison.
